summary: Pass 1 selected because only the original sample path was supplied and no unpack report was named. Static analysis identifies a 64-bit Windows PE apphost/self-contained .NET runtime carrier for officecli.dll rather than a conventional packed malware loader. The native entry follows wmainCRTStartup -> __scrt_common_main_seh -> main -> exe_start; exe_start references the bundled managed application name officecli.dll and calls hostfxr_main_bundle_startupinfo. Large code and string volume comes from embedded CoreCLR/runtime and Brotli components. Imports include memory mapping/protection, process, registry, named-pipe diagnostics, and debugger APIs, but observed references are consistent with .NET hosting/runtime behavior. No dynamic execution was performed. A second unpack/recovery phase is recommended only if downstream stages need to extract the bundled managed payload officecli.dll for managed-code inspection, not because an unpack stub was confirmed.

findings.title: Sample is a 64-bit .NET apphost
findings.description: The file is a 64-bit PE with a CLR-heavy import table and apphost startup flow consistent with a .NET application host.
findings.reasoning: Survey data shows x64 PE layout, a large .text/.rdata footprint, and many CoreCLR/runtime symbols and strings. The main function calls exe_start, which references hostfxr_main_startupinfo and System.Private.CoreLib.dll, confirming managed startup.

evidence.observation: Architecture 64, image base 0x140000000, hash 937db176b585e874aa5bff48d536bce78037665cd862b5deefe56e79977e6588, and numerous CoreCLR-related symbols/strings were present.
main calls exe_start, and exe_start references hostfxr_main_startupinfo, hostfxr_main_bundle_startupinfo, and System.Private.CoreLib.dll.

findings.title: Execution follows the standard native hostfxr startup path
findings.description: The native entry path is the normal CRT startup sequence into a hostfxr-based .NET bootstrapper rather than a custom self-unpacking loader.
findings.reasoning: wmainCRTStartup enters __scrt_common_main_seh, which calls main. main sets up tracing, redirects buffered errors, and calls exe_start. exe_start performs host path resolution and invokes hostfxr_main_startupinfo / hostfxr_main_bundle_startupinfo, indicating apphost-driven managed startup.

evidence.observation: Startup is the standard CRT trampoline into __scrt_common_main_seh.
exe_start resolves app_path, dotnet_root, and host_path, then calls hostfxr_main_startupinfo and hostfxr_main_bundle_startupinfo.

findings.title: No strong custom packer indicators found
findings.description: Static indicators favor a large managed runtime host over a custom packer or decryptor stub.
findings.reasoning: The binary contains extensive CoreCLR symbols, many managed runtime strings, and a large normal import surface for file, process, registry, and COM operations. The observed entry flow is consistent with a .NET host and does not show a compact decode loop, staged memory mapping stub, or obvious import-resolving shellcode loader.

evidence.observation: Interesting strings include CoreCLR exception/runtime markers, diagnostics IPC messages, and System.Private.CoreLib.dll.

Imports include VirtualAlloc, VirtualProtect, CreateProcessW, GetProcAddress, LoadLibraryA/W, IsDebuggerPresent, and many runtime/COM/file APIs, but the overall profile remains consistent with a host application rather than a tiny unpacker stub.

limitations: A managed payload can still contain behavior of interest after host startup; native indicators alone do not exclude later-stage obfuscation inside managed assemblies.

artifacts.context: Primary analyzed sample; IDB open and survey completed successfully.

investigation_targets.reason: Trace the error-writer redirection in main to confirm where diagnostics buffering is installed before exe_start.
investigation_targets.recommended_action: Set a breakpoint on the trace writer assignment and inspect the resulting writer callback path.
investigation_targets.success_criteria: Confirm the buffered-error sink and whether it influences later control flow or only logging.

investigation_targets.reason: Observe the hostfxr startup handoff inside exe_start, especially the call site(s) that resolve the runtime and bundle path.
investigation_targets.recommended_action: Break on hostfxr_main_startupinfo and hostfxr_main_bundle_startupinfo or their immediate call sites.
investigation_targets.success_criteria: Identify the managed payload handoff and any runtime parameters used to launch the .NET application.

investigation_targets.reason: Check the dynamic TLS initialization gate to determine whether any runtime callbacks are registered before managed entry.
investigation_targets.recommended_action: Break on the dynamic TLS init callback and record whether it only initializes runtime helpers.
investigation_targets.success_criteria: Confirm TLS callbacks are runtime scaffolding rather than custom unpack logic.

investigation_targets.reason: Verify the transition from CRT startup into the common main path.
investigation_targets.recommended_action: Break just after _security_init_cookie and before the call into __scrt_common_main_seh.
investigation_targets.success_criteria: Confirm standard CRT startup and exclude an alternate entry trampoline.

limitations: The sample appears to be a managed apphost, so the meaningful payload likely lives in managed assemblies or runtime-loaded content not fully visible in the native apphost analysis.
No dynamic execution was performed, so runtime-decoded content and post-launch managed behaviors remain unconfirmed.
The import list is broad and includes APIs that may be inherited from the runtime rather than used directly by malicious logic.

reasons: Static evidence indicates a standard .NET apphost bootstrap rather than a bespoke native packer.
The file already exposes managed runtime startup markers and hostfxr handoff strings instead of a narrow decode loop or memory-mapping stub.
If unpacking is needed later, it is more likely to be managed-assembly extraction than native stub recovery.
